title: Foundational Babylonian Advocates Division: Among the Dispersion

sense.text:
“Why do the heathen rage, and the people imagine a vain thing?” The heathen here are the other nations: the so-called white man in particular, the Roman Empire in its day, and the same power now.

This is the premise behind the whole class. A movement has grown among the so-called African-Americans called FBA, foundational black American: a black person whose ancestry goes back to the 1800s here in the South, not an immigrant, not from the Caribbean, not Hispanic, not from the continent of Africa. They use fancy words like ethnogenesis, meaning your racial beginning is here, and delineation, meaning drawing the line: we are black Americans over here, and you Caribbean blacks and you blacks from the continent are over there. Some of them hate the Caribbean blacks and the continental blacks and use white nationalist talking points against their own people, who were enslaved outside this country by the same exact man.

That is displaced anger: an anger black folks cannot execute towards the white man, so they execute it towards their brothers from the islands and their brothers from the continent. It is a temper tantrum thrown by a people who still do not understand that we are the children of Israel according to the Bible. First it was African-American, then Afro-American, now FBA: another byword we have given ourselves. A foundational Babylonian advocate, because these people love it here. And the year 1526 they claim means nothing; no one was calling themselves foundational black Americans in 1526.

“The kings of the earth set themselves”: that is the so-called white man prophesied of here, in the time of Rome and now. “And the rulers take counsel together”: the rulers are our own people, our own political leaders and spokesmen. Not your rulers, but rulers over us all the same.

They set themselves “against the Lord, and against his anointed”: against the Lord and his Son, and in another sense against the Lord, his Son and his disciples.

“Let us break their bands asunder”: the bands are this Bible. This Bible is the only book that can bring about a global unity among our people, scattered through the four corners of the earth, and only when used by its rightful owners and teachers to band the children of Israel, all twelve tribes, back together again.

That is why the class is called Division Among the Dispersion: we are the dispersed, we are the diaspora, and the word itself comes from the Bible concerning our people, the scattered Israelites all over the world. The moment you see a movement that hinders, slows down or thwarts that coming together, it is of Satan, immediately.

“And cast away their cords from us”: the cords are the word of God, the words of the Lord and of the prophets. That is what our people do not want, and what the so-called white man does not want brought to our people, wherever we are.

“If thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes”, “all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee.” These are the conditions of the covenant. Had we kept God's commandments, the blessings of the first verses would have come on us; we chose the opposite, and so we received the curses from verse 15 down.

“Cursed shalt thou be in the city”: the ghettos and slums, crime, poverty, low reading levels and illiteracy, degeneracy, poor housing, roaches, bed bugs, water bugs and rats. That is the black community. Not everywhere, but you will find a black ghetto everywhere. You do not find Arab ghettos everywhere, or Russian, Hawaiian or Asian ghettos. You find black and brown people, whether you call it the barrio, the shack town, the ghetto or the reservation.

“And cursed shalt thou be in the field”: the plantations. Cursed in the rubber fields of Africa, in the rice fields, the cotton fields, the indigo, tobacco and sugarcane fields, all through the Americas and all through the continent of Africa wherever it was colonized.

“The Lord shall smite thee with madness”: craziness, mental illness, mental dysfunction, psychological trauma. When slavery ended we got no medication and no therapist. No nation could undergo what we underwent, in North, South or Central America or on the continent, and still have any sanity left. Men come back from war with PTSD; we went through 400 years of torture, hangings, lynchings and castrations, then Jim Crow, convict leasing, black codes, redlining and the KKK, and the lynching has not stopped. It is proven that slavery mutated our DNA: the trauma is embedded in us genetically, from what our forefathers saw, tarred and feathered, torn apart between horses, raped in front of their families on the bottom of a slave ship that some stupid black people now deny ever existed.

That is the madness: black folks love everything that hates us. We want to be Indians because white folks love Indians, and love Egypt because white folks love Egypt. We will hug the murderer of our own brother and hand her a Bible. Yet where are the sundown towns of the Jamaicans? Where are the Haitians hanging black Americans in Mississippi? There are none, but all the animosity is pointed at people who look like you, while white folks hang us wholesale in the South and nobody says anything.

“And blindness”: you do not know who you are, where you are from, or who your God is. Lost and confused.

“Thou shalt betroth a wife, and another man shall lie with her”: our women were raped in front of us.

“Thou shalt build an house, and thou shalt not dwell therein”: we built America and its foundation, the White House, the monuments, the Capitol. Benjamin Banneker was instrumental in the Capitol, though unfortunately he was involved in sorcery. We built it, but we did not live in it until Obama got there.

“Thou shalt plant a vineyard, and shalt not gather the grapes thereof”: the fields again, and colonization: growing your own crops for somebody else who does not belong in your land. Native Americans experienced this too.

Those who deny the slave ships should ask one question: were there cargo ships before slavery? The Europeans robbed Africa of silver, gold, diamonds and rubber. How did they carry it? There were no trains or planes. By boat, the same boats they put us in the bottom of. When slavery ended they did not throw the boats away; they used them for what they were used for before.

“Thine ox shall be slain before thine eyes, and thou shalt not eat thereof”: the Native Americans, who are our people, had land here, and some were reclassified as Negroes to lose it. It was a paper genocide: the I for Indian was written over into an N for Negro, and the land was lost.

“Thine ass shall be violently taken away from before thy face, and shall not be restored to thee”: the forty acres and a mule. You are not getting it back; “restored” goes to reparations. They can drop bomb upon bomb on Iran, but there is no money for the Negro.

“Thy sheep shall be given unto thine enemies”: your resources and your land given to your enemies, not to you.

“Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people, and thine eyes shall look, and fail with longing for them all the day long”: our children were snatched out of our arms on the auction block and given to somebody else against our will. We cried and mourned for them and never saw them again, as when they took Kizzy in Roots, and Eliza in 12 Years a Slave, who cried the whole time for the children she lost.

“Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but thou shalt not enjoy them; for they shall go into captivity”: this happened to our people historically. They were snatched out of our arms and given to somebody else.

“The stranger that is within thee shall get up above thee very high; and thou shalt come down very low”: that is the Berlin Conference and the carving up of Africa. The Arabs ransacked the top half of the continent first, and the Portuguese came after them in the 1400s as rivals in the slave trade. How did they get there, if there were no ships?

“He shall lend to thee, and thou shalt not lend to him”: Africa is the richest land mass on the planet. They walk on copper and gold there; it is called the Gold Coast for a reason, and Zambia sits on a copper belt, yet our brothers cannot export their own resources, and the Arabs oversee the mining. If the money in Africa were backed by what is in its ground, everyone there would be a billionaire, but the white man says your money is worth nothing. The world depends on that continent; when our people there cut off France's uranium, France plots to attack.

It is rich because God's people are in there. Wherever God's people are found you find the same resources and abundance. That is what brought Columbus, Cortez, Balboa and Amerigo Vespucci here, and the Portuguese, French, Germans and Dutch over there: to rob God's people.

“He shall be the head, and thou shalt be the tail”: wherever you are, he rules over you and you are on the bottom.

“Moreover all these curses shall come upon thee, and shall pursue thee, and overtake thee”: wherever we run, the curses follow behind us, to Europe, to Africa, to the Americas, “till thou be destroyed; because thou hearkenedst not unto the voice of the Lord thy God.”

“And they shall be upon thee for a sign”: these curses are the designation of who and where God's people are in these last days. When you travel, and some of you running your mouths have no passport, you find these curses on our people wherever they are.

“And upon thy seed for ever”: generational curses, not one-time curses, upon our children until God says it is enough.

We did not serve the Lord “with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things”, so we serve our enemies “in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things.” For food, water and clothing we rely on the so-called white man, the European system, or the Arab or Asian system, depending on the land you are in. Whatever you lack, you let your enemy provide.

“And he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck”: all nations did this, the Arabs too, but the white man primarily. The chains have been removed, but they are still there in the mind and the thought process. That is the madness of verse 28: a mind in prison, not thinking logically.

“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other”: we are the dispersed, the diaspora. A destroyed mind does not know who it is, hates its own kind, and turns on its own brothers who were conquered and destroyed just like you.

“And there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known”: Christianity and Islam.

“And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships”: into bondage again, not with imaginary ships, not with planes, trains or a hot air balloon. With ships. That is what Moses was told to tell us.

“By the way whereof I spake unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again”: you will never see that Egypt as slaves again. That one you walked into; this Egypt is by boats.

“And there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen”: sold off those ships as slave men and slave women to the same enemies of verse 48 who put the yoke of iron on our necks. It all connects.

“And no man shall buy you”: the first time, Moses saved us, and we had Samson and Gideon. This slavery, no man can end. Not Nat Turner, not Gabriel Prosser, not Toussaint, not Dessalines, not Nanny, not Medgar Evers, not Martin, not Malcolm. God says, I will do it: Christ comes down to save us, and no one else.

precepts.why:
“I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.” Egypt is the house of bondage, the house of slavery and captivity. Egypt and slavery are synonymous.

So when Deuteronomy 28:68 says the Lord shall bring us “into Egypt again with ships”, it means into slavery again, and this time by ships.

sense.text:
“If they sin against thee, (for there is no man that sinneth not,) and thou be angry with them, and deliver them to the enemy”: he did, by ships. “So that they carry them away captives unto the land of the enemy”: this is the land of our enemy. Our enemy conquered us and made this land, which was once ours, his land.

“Far or near”: far from Jerusalem, as we are now, or near it, in Africa or Madagascar, colonized all the same.

“Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives”: bethink means to remember, to call to mind. Solomon in his prayer saw in the spirit us put on those ships and scattered all over the world, yokes on our necks, destroyed so badly that we would turn our eyes against our own people and attack them.

The Portuguese got into Africa in the 1400s, the Canary Islands first, and with Jesuit missionaries brainwashed the Hamites and the Israelites on that continent, mostly us, because Satan showed them where we are. Six hundred years of colonization, and the white man became god over there and god over here. So the brother who comes from there thinks we are nothing, and that is where the disrespect comes from. There are coons everywhere, from the continent, from the Caribbean and from here, because the same colonizers brainwashed us on both sides of the world. Black America roasts its own: we mocked the brother from Mali who could not speak English, and he went to college while we stood on the corner. You cannot get mad at it; just do better. We do it to them all the time, and when the tables turn we want to cut them off.

“And repent, and make supplication unto thee”, “saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness”: we can only do that if we know who we are. Solomon saw that in the long run we would end up in captivity and lose our identity, try to become something else and not recreate ourselves in the image of God. That is why we must bethink, remember, ourselves.

precepts.why:
Baruch makes the word bethink plain: “For I knew that they would not hear me, because it is a stiffnecked people: but in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves.” That is why he put us in captivity: we would not hear.

In the land of our captivity, the land of our enemy, we shall remember ourselves. To bethink themselves in 1 Kings 8:47 is to remember who we are.

sense.text:
“And thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword”. A proverb is the slick saying our brothers from Haiti and Jamaica have about us: you are lazy, you do not take care of your kids, you are criminals. Some of these proverbs are true, and if you have lived it and seen it you cannot get mad.

A byword is a person, thing or phrase deeply tied to a quality or idea. FBA is a byword. African-American is a byword. Jamaican, Trinidadian, Haitian, Puerto Rican, Dominican, Sierra Leonean, Nigerian, Malagasy, Native American, Indian: all bywords. Names given to us outside our God-given name, whether we gave them to ourselves or they were forced upon us. They are not our names.

In the Bible a byword is an object of scorn and ridicule, a shocking example of divine judgment, a national disgrace among the nations for breaking the covenant. That is the condition of the black man and woman all over the world today.

“Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired”: we are a nation not desired. We are wanted for entertainment, to make someone laugh or cry, to throw a ball, run, jump, fight, tell a joke or sing; outside of that they have no need for us at all.

When God says gather together, he means gather together as Israelites: not as FBA, not as African-Americans.

“Before the decree bring forth”, “before the day of the Lord’s anger come upon you”: God is saying, gather yourselves together before this happens.

The root of this whole FBA thing is that black people believe America will last forever. So they pride themselves on being here from the beginning, the foundation: we have always been here, I was in the house first, if it weren't for me you couldn't come in the house. That is house talk: the talk of one who boasts he was in the house first.

But here is not home. The Native Americans, Israelites, came here as a place of refuge and exile when the northern kingdom was deported out of its land and could not return. Home is the land of Israel, from the Nile to the Euphrates; that is the land mass Israel is warring over today. America is not our home.

“Seek ye the Lord”: this Bible should be your foundation. “All ye meek of the earth”: submit yourselves to the word of God. “Which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness”: seek to keep God's commandments, and righteousness goes back to loving your neighbour as yourself, which we cannot even do. “It may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord’s anger.”

precepts.why:
“Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!” That is the gathering together God calls for in Zephaniah.

“It is like the precious ointment upon the head, that ran down upon the beard, even Aaron’s beard.” The Lord compares the unity of our people to the anointing oil poured on Aaron's head, which only Aaron and his sons could wear; whoever copied or mimicked it was put to death. That is how precious and exclusive that oil was, and so is our unity. A European Union or an African summit of Hamites is nothing in the eyes of God. The unity God seeks is the unity of all twelve tribes of Israel scattered through the world, especially on the continent of Africa where we are abundant.

That is revolutionary thinking: global and international. You cannot be domestic and call yourself revolutionary. Malcolm X said the same: we catch hell not because we are Baptist or Methodist, Democrat or Republican, but because we are black, ex-slaves brought here in chains by the people who came on the Mayflower. When you stop thinking you are an American, you start showing signs of intelligence.

As long as you do not know who you are, you will never know who your enemy is. You will make your enemy yourself, your own people from the continent or the Caribbean, and the white man gets a pass. Delineate yourself from the Fourth of July, Christmas and Thanksgiving, from the white god you worship on Sundays, from another woman's hair on your head, from the $500 sneakers and the designer clothes. Even our diet of three meals a day is Edom's portions. That is the real tethering.

sense.text:
Not that we should not wear the clothes our enemies provide; but to go out of our way for the most expensive of their clothes, a Dolce & Gabbana belt or a Fendi bag while working at Walmart with rent due, is tethering. Esau waits until it goes on sale, or goes to Marshalls and the thrift shop; a millionaire like Adam Sandler walks around in regular clothes and gym shorts. We walk through a poor neighbourhood in gold and platinum, put a stack of money to our ear on social media and tell everyone where we live, and when they come to the door we cry for justice. That is a destroyed mind, madness, and more than likely another dadless household.

“And I will set my face against you, and ye shall be slain before your enemies: they that hate you shall reign over you”: you will know who your enemies are, because they will rule over you.

“And ye shall flee when none pursueth you”: you run and cower when no one pursues you. The Most High put a cowardly spirit upon us. It is a slave mind that focuses all its anger on a people oppressed and destroyed just like you: displaced anger. The coons, Jason Whitlock and Brandon Tatum, say I make millions, I am no slave; they do not know who the enemy is.

precepts.why:
“And I will break the pride of your power”: you will be powerless. “And I will make your heaven as iron, and your earth as brass”: put in chains.

The enemy that reigns over us in verse 17 holds that power; we have none.

“I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies; and the sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them”: cowardice. That is why the rappers talk about their ops, and the gangs, Crips, Bloods, Hoovers, will never set foot in white neighbourhoods and terrorize them. And those who talk to their ancestors and their crystals: why don't the ancestors tell us who killed our people and who did the lynchings?

“And ye shall have no power to stand before your enemies.” You have to know who your enemies are; that is why we have no power. Our power is the Lord, and we turned against that power. We will cry, protest and march, but there is no power until we repent, and so it will keep happening.

sense.text:
Malcolm X said at Bandung the colonized nations kept the white man out and settled their little quarrels among themselves; when you have a family squabble you do not take it to the sidewalk. Christ was revolutionary and said the same thing.

“Therefore if thou bring thy gift to the altar, and there rememberest that thy brother hath ought against thee”: before you bring your sacrifice, you remember your brother has a problem with you. “Leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother”: leave the sacrifice, go and make up with your brother, reconcile whatever problem you have. “And then come and offer thy gift.”

We do the opposite: we go on social media and announce our problems with the Haitians or the Jamaicans for the world to see.

precepts.why:
That is where Christ got it from. “Go not forth hastily to strive”: to argue, to fight. “Debate thy cause with thy neighbour himself; and discover not a secret to another”: do not announce it, do not gossip, do not run around telling anybody your problem with your brother. “Lest he that heareth it put thee to shame, and thine infamy turn not away.”

Go to your brother, and him alone, and deal with it. We do not do that as a people; we want attention, views, likes and money. Remove Edom from our conversations and deal with each other. That is our problem: we want Edom involved in everything we do and say.

sense.text: “Arise ye, and depart; for this is not your rest”: this is not our home. We are not free here; we are here because we are not free. “Because it is polluted”: this land is polluted. “It shall destroy you, even with a sore destruction”: you will die with it.

precepts.why:
“Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail”: that is what we are doing now, in pain and labour to bring forth the word of God. “Thou shalt dwell in the field”: captivity. “And thou shalt go even to Babylon; there shalt thou be delivered”: saved from our enemies in Babylon, in captivity, by our God.

“There the Lord shall redeem thee from the hand of thine enemies.” That is why no man shall buy us: the Lord himself will buy us. Redeem means to buy again. Not any man.

So depart from this place; it is not your rest. We are not Americans; we are the children of Israel, God's chosen people, and the tribe of Judah is in America. America is temporary, a confinement. Malcolm said it: I was in prison, and you are still in prison; that is what America means. Not foundational black American, foundational black prisoner. In the Schomburg Center in Harlem his Bible lies open inside his Quran at Psalms 83: he knew who he was.

sense.text: “Before I go whence I shall not return”: the captivity we go into. “Even to the land of darkness and the shadow of death”: this land, Babylon, America, is called the land of darkness and the shadow of death.

“A land of darkness, as darkness itself”: America is as darkness itself. “Without any order”: chaos and discord are celebrated here. “And where the light is as darkness”: good is seen as evil and sin is seen as good. That is what Negroes brag about being foundationally a part of.

precepts.why:
“Behold, we are yet this day in our captivity, where thou hast scattered us, for a reproach and a curse, and to be subject to payments, according to all the iniquities of our fathers”: we are in captivity even now. “Hear, Israel, the commandments of life: give ear to understand wisdom.”

“How happeneth it Israel, that thou art in thine enemies’ land”: as Solomon said, the land of the enemy. “That thou art waxen old”: waxed old and weak. The men and women of the sixties are nowhere near the caliber of the men and women today. Ask a young one who Kwame Ture, Jean-Jacques Dessalines, Medgar Evers, Stokely Carmichael or Huey P. Newton were and he does not know, but he knows every athlete and rapper. Generation Z, for zombie.

“In a strange country”: America is that strange country, the land of darkness as darkness itself in Job. “That thou art defiled with the dead”: we are a spiritually dead people, zombies, lost in displaced anger and ignorance, saying we were always here and there were no slave ships. That mindset means you read nothing.

sense.text: “And set me down in the midst of the valley which was full of bones”: a valley full of bones is a graveyard. It is the same strange land where Baruch said we waxed old and were defiled with the dead.
Ezekiel was made to walk round about the bones, “very many in the open valley; and, lo, they were very dry”: no nourishment, no understanding, no water.
“Son of man, can these bones live? And I answered, O Lord God, thou knowest”: I do not know; you know.

“Prophesy upon these bones”: teach these bones. “O ye dry bones, hear the word of the Lord”: what must be brought to these bones is the word of God. Not the word of some hustler, ex-pimp, pastor, preacher or rapper, but the words of the Bible.

“Behold, I will cause breath to enter into you”: the breath is the word of God, “and ye shall live.”

“And I will lay sinews upon you, and will bring up flesh upon you”: the sinews and flesh are your identity, how you look and who you are. When you hear the word of God you learn your identity; you bethink, remember, yourselves. The word of God grants understanding of who you are, and nothing outside of it. “And ye shall know that I am the Lord.”

“The bones came together, bone to his bone.” “The sinews and the flesh came up upon them”, “but there was no breath in them.” That was Malcolm's time, the turbulent sixties, when our people were seeking identity, unifying and coming together, but not through the word of God. Flesh and sinews were on us, but no breath yet. Now we are in the time when life is in us and we are slowly standing up; it is a process of time.

“Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live.” “And they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.” That is the unity Malcolm was talking about: standing together as one, one mind, one understanding, one God, one race, one nation, not divided. That is the army God is slowly raising up among us, an empire within an empire, and eyes are on us.

precepts.why:
“Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.” Not a rap lyric: it is in the Bible.

The valley of the shadow of death is the same darkness Job spoke of in Job 10:21-22, and the same valley full of bones in Ezekiel 37.

“The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.” When we were conquered, overthrown and colonized by our oppressors, over the course of time up until now, we wandered out of understanding, and now we are the congregation of the dead.

We are a spiritually dead people, alive and well, but inside dead, destroyed, divisive, self-defeating and self-hating. Those are the dry bones of the valley, waxed old and defiled with the dead.

sense.text: “To open the blind eyes, to bring out the prisoners from the prison”: America is your prison. “And them that sit in darkness out of the prison house”: those that sit in darkness are in the same land as Job 10, the valley of dry bones, the valley of the shadow of death. The Bible calls the lands of our captivity prisons and prison houses.

precepts.why:
“But this is a people robbed and spoiled”: that is us. “They are all of them snared in holes”: religious holes, philosophical holes, political holes, identity holes. “And they are hid in prison houses”: spiritual prison houses, the physical prison houses of mass incarceration too, but primarily the prison of our minds.

“They are for a prey”: exploited, extorted, used and abused. “And none delivereth”: no one is trying to save us; God said, I will come and redeem you, no one but me. “For a spoil, and none saith, Restore”: no one says restore the spirit back into those bones. They leave them dead.

“In an acceptable time have I heard thee, and in a day of salvation have I helped thee”: he will save us. “And give thee for a covenant of the people, to establish the earth”: God is going to use us to establish law and order on this earth. “To cause to inherit the desolate heritages”: our land back.

“That thou mayest say to the prisoners, Go forth; to them that are in darkness, Shew yourselves”: the prisoners in the prison house of Isaiah 42 brought out. “Their pastures shall be in all high places”: we shall get the kingdom, out of prison and into the kingdom.

Malcolm said there is no such thing as a nonviolent revolution, and land is the basis of all independence. When the dry bones come together and keep God's commandments, we will turn away from the system and it will bring persecution. The whole premise of getting our land back is bloodshed: the Lord will come back, destroy our enemies and put us back in our land. But it is not by might nor by power but by his spirit; this is spiritual warfare, and this man deals with Satan directly. J. Edgar Hoover said the greatest threat to America is Negro unity, not foundational black American unity.

sense.text: “Woe be to the shepherds of Israel that do feed themselves! should not the shepherds feed the flocks?”: shepherds who get rich, make money and feed themselves.

“Ye eat the fat”: you eat well, you live well. “And ye clothe you with the wool”: you dress in fancy clothes. “Ye kill them that are fed: but ye feed not the flock”: an abundance of food and resources, and you do not feed your own people.
“Neither have ye brought again that which was driven away”: the scattered and conquered. “Neither have ye sought that which was lost; but with force and with cruelty have ye ruled them.”
“And they were scattered, because there is no shepherd”: we were scattered because there was no leader. “And they became meat to all the beasts of the field”: we were conquered and overthrown.

“My sheep wandered through all the mountains”: we were dispersed. “My flock was scattered upon all the face of the earth, and none did search or seek after them.” A shepherd's job is to go out, search and seek his sheep, his people, all over the world if possible.

“Neither did my shepherds search for my flock, but the shepherds fed themselves, and fed not my flock”: that is your pastor today. They do not feed their people, and they look for Israel in one place only while feeding themselves. You have to search and seek your people who are scattered. That is a global revolution.

Malcolm said a revolutionary is a black nationalist; he wants a nation. The two go hand in hand: to be revolutionary you have to deal with your people worldwide. Even a historian of Caesar and Christ wrote that Christ was, in a spiritual sense, the greatest revolutionist in history. Christ is the greatest black nationalist in history: he cared for Israel scattered all over the world, not only in Jerusalem, and sent his apostles out to find their people. Calling the brothers over there Hamites just means you are broke and cannot travel.

“And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation.” A holy nation: black national, black nationalism, revolutionary. “These are the words which thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel.” Israel is a nation of people.
Christ is about black nationalism on a global scale. “As the Father knoweth me, even so know I the Father: and I lay down my life for the sheep.”

“And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold”: Israel scattered abroad. “Them also I must bring.” Christ did not deal only with his own people Judah, who are the African-Americans today. He did not say, I will save Judah only and delineate myself from the other tribes. He said he must unite all twelve, not just one tribe in America that is mad over words.

“And they shall hear my voice”: God's people will hear his voice, whether you think they are Ham or not. “And there shall be one fold, and one shepherd”: one nation and one leader.

precepts.why:
Caiaphas said “that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.” That one man is Christ, who dealt with the whole nation.

“He prophesied that Jesus should die for that nation; And not for that nation only”: not for Judah, the African-Americans, the FBA, only. “But that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad.” Christ had to bring together all Israel scattered abroad. That is the other sheep of John 10:16, and that is a global black nationalism.

sense.text: For the Negroes who say we have always been here. “Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land”: the northern kingdom was conquered by Assyria, “and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.”

“But they took this counsel among themselves”: they got the freedom to do so from Persia. “That they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go forth into a further country”: that is here. “That they might there keep their statutes, which they never kept in their own land”: some of them did and some did not. “Their own land”: that is how we know this land is exile.

“And the same region is called Arsareth”: that is America today, the new found land. They left, came here, could not go back to their own land, and came to keep the laws they never kept there. It lets you know this is temporary. It was the land set for us to be in for these times: to be overthrown and enslaved in, and to be saved out of while it burns. This is not our land. That is why it is going to burn.

“Behold, the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we: Come on, let us deal wisely with them; lest they multiply”: Egypt plotted to destroy us. We were growing in number and becoming a threat to them.
“Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens. And they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses”: we built the Valley of the Kings.
“But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew”: the more they gave us hell, the more we grew. “And they were grieved because of the children of Israel”: they could not stop us.

“And the Egyptians made the children of Israel to serve with rigour”: to serve with severity. The rigour of verse 13 is the hard bondage of verse 14, in mortar, brick and all manner of service in the field.

From verse 15 down they said kill all the males: that is Planned Parenthood and population control, Margaret Sanger, and verse 10 is her plan: deal wisely with them. When they could not kill us with hard labour and bondage, they started killing the babies. Nothing new under the sun; they did it here too.

“And when the people complained, it displeased the Lord”: saved out of hard bondage and the murder of our babies by Moses, and we complained. “And the fire of the Lord burnt among them”: God set us on fire.

“And the mixt multitude that was among them fell a lusting”: heathen who came out with us and were among us. “And the children of Israel also wept again, and said, Who shall give us flesh to eat?”: following behind the other nations, while they were already eating.

“We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely”: they were not free; they worked with rigour. But the slave mind was still there. “The cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlick: But now our soul is dried away”: they reminisced about slavery and how good they ate in bondage, like remembering how good the Popeyes and the McDonald's were. Foundational black Egyptians.

“And all the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron”: they complained, and said “Would God that we had died in the land of Egypt!” They were free, and wished they had died in slavery.

“Were it not better for us to return into Egypt?”: let us go back to massa. Stockholm syndrome. “Let us make a captain”: let us find a Brandon Tatum, a Jason Whitlock, “and let us return into Egypt”, back to slavery.

That goes back to being destroyed, and it is the same with us here. Tell them America is Babylon the great and they say no: we have always been here, we are Americans, we eat good, live good and dress good. The same mentality.

precepts.why:
“For my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water.”

“Is Israel a servant? is he a homeborn slave?” Even God asks the question. A homeborn slave is a slave born in the house. “Why is he spoiled?” Why is he always destroyed? Because we are always breaking God's laws and will not do what God said to do. We are about to go back to slavery because we are homeborn slaves, the same as those who wanted a captain to take them back into Egypt.

sense.text:
“Because ye have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement”: we have made a covenant with America because we want to stay here forever. America will give us money and we will live good, eat good, the garlic, the melons and the leeks again. Reparations: how much, and where is the plan? There is no plan; it is just talk.

“When the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto us”: when America is being destroyed, no problems will come our way, we think.

“For we have made lies our refuge, and under falsehood have we hid ourselves”: the falsehood is a false identity, false titles, lies about how we got here and our origins. We hide under it until death comes.

precepts.why:
“Let us go and make a covenant with the heathen that are round about us: for since we departed from them we have had much sorrow.” We must always have massa around.

That is the foundational mind: all we have to do is stay here, be patient and quiet, and massa will give us money because he knows we deserve it. “So this device pleased them well. Then certain of the people were so forward herein, that they went to the king.” The same covenant with death of Isaiah 28:15.

sense.text: “And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free”: free from spiritual captivity, and from physical captivity after that.

“We be Abraham’s seed, and were never in bondage to any man”: we are not slaves to nobody. I make six figures, I live in the suburbs, I make ten million a year, I am a spokesman, a politician, I have my amendment rights. “How sayest thou, Ye shall be made free?” What do you mean? We are already free.

precepts.why:
John 11 shows they were liars. “Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council”, and said “the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.” The Romans, the white men, would come and take away their authority and remove them out of the land.

Among themselves they understood they were not free; they knew they were captive. They said they were never in bondage, yet feared Rome would remove them from their seat of authority. They were lying for the audience.

sense.text:
“The sceptre shall not depart from Judah”: the so-called African-Americans today are the tribe of Judah, the head tribe, starting with Christ. “Nor a lawgiver from between his feet”: we are the ones who establish the law, because Christ is the lawgiver. “Until Shiloh come”: Christ is Shiloh.

“And unto him shall the gathering of the people be”: unto Christ shall be the gathering of all twelve tribes. Not the dividing, not the foundational ones: the gathering of the nation Israel, starting with the teaching coming from Judah. We will be the ones to go out through the world, find our people and unite us all in these laws and commandments as Israelites, not as foundational Babylonian Americans, or later foundational burnt Americans. If you do not repent and keep these commandments, you will burn with America.

precepts.why:
“And this is the blessing of Judah: and he said, Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him unto his people.” That is Ezekiel 34: going out to search and seek them. Judah will be the tribe to go out first and foremost and search for the other tribes.

It was written long ago that the Negroes of the United States are the most advanced section of the Negro population of the world, destined to be the vanguard of the liberation of the Negro masses on an international scale. That is Judah. We are going to find Israel all over the world.
